findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects including the uploaded vendor roster are stored without an enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 default.

No ACL is declared and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, leaving protection against accidental public ACL or bucket-policy grants dependent on account-level defaults.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so sensitive financial export data is stored without an enforced default encryption policy.
The bucket relies on a private canned ACL only; no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so a later policy or ACL change could expose ledger exports publicly.
The model artifact bucket enables versioning and logging but omits server_side_encryption_configuration, so artifacts are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the bucket, leaving it dependent on account defaults to block public ACLs and policies.

The runbook bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks commonly contain sensitive internal procedures and credential references and are stored without enforced encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so nothing in this configuration prevents a public ACL or policy from being applied to the runbook bucket.

findings.issue_category: invalid canned ACL on log bucket
findings.description: The acl value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid canned ACL (apparently a corrupted "log-delivery-write"), so the intended log-delivery grant is malformed and the effective access control on the audit log bucket is not what was intended.

The audit log bucket sets force_destroy = true with no object lock or MFA delete, so the entire audit trail and its versions can be deleted by a single apply or a compromised credential, undermining non-repudiation of the logs.
The bucket holding audit logs has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, leaving the log data exposed to accidental public ACL or policy grants.

The vendor roster spreadsheet (likely third-party business data/PII) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that itself defines no default encryption, so it is stored unencrypted.
